family_relationship.identity: Cruising Task Force Findings & Recommendations (per R-17-250), dated April 2, 2018, is a City of Albuquerque City Council Cruising Task Force report. The cover and running headers identify the City Council body; the acknowledgements identify 11 named participants from car clubs, merchants, City Planning, APD, DMD, Cultural Services, and City Council Services.
family_relationship.resolution_relationship: Appendix C reproduces City Council Bill R-17-250, enacted as R-2017-113 and sponsored by Klarissa Peña and Isaac Benton. That resolution establishes the 10-member task force to explore options and make recommendations to promote responsible cruising. The report documents six February-March meetings and supplies the resulting findings and recommendations; it is the task force's substantive completion of that charge, not the resolution itself.
family_relationship.finality: The cover calls the work Findings & Recommendations; its executive summary, complete two-part structure, prioritized next steps, and appendices confirm a finished deliverable. Appendix H labels only its proposed economic-impact-analysis scope preliminary; that limited future-work component does not make the report a draft.

No alternate authoritative version or stronger canonical report was found or inferred.

quality_assessment.visual_inspection: Rendered cover, acknowledgements/membership, a recommendation page, Appendix C's R-17-250 page, and the economic-impact appendix. The professionally designed City Council report has legible text, photographs, tables/structured recommendations, and consistent headers/footers; no material rendering defect was observed.
quality_assessment.measured_content: 43 letter pages; 9,756,353 bytes; 14,455 extracted words. Part 1 covers local and national cruising history, task-force establishment, methodology, and existing conditions. Part 2 supplies legislative, administrative, event-coordination, enforcement, economic-development, next-step, and vision recommendations. Appendices preserve the governing ordinance/resolutions, comparative research, proposed economic-analysis scope, survey/results, and bibliography.
quality_assessment.standalone_public_value: High. It is a dated City Council task-force deliverable on a distinctive Albuquerque transportation, cultural-heritage, public-safety, and downtown policy question, retaining both the deliberative basis and actionable recommendations.
quality_assessment.information_density: High: approximately 336 extracted words per page, with substantive narrative, prioritized recommendations, documented methodology, a survey, and primary legal/context appendices. It is not a skeletal presentation, attachment, or administrative fragment.
quality_assessment.series_component_relationship: A self-contained final report, not a serial installment. Its embedded copies of O-05-104, R-05-328, and R-17-250 are contextual appendices rather than a reason to classify the report as a duplicate of those legal records.
quality_assessment.intended_publication_form: After separately authorized unchanged R2 archival and public-byte verification, retain it as one standalone original under the Transportation landing page's future City transportation policy/history material. Do not split or repackage the report; preserve its original 43-page container and direct City provenance.
quality_assessment.rationale: Its complete final-report form, City Council provenance, strong measured and visual content, unique policy recommendations, and lack of a stronger canonical version meet the AGENTS.md publication-quality threshold. This approval is inventory-only and does not authorize archive or visible publication work.
